summary: Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1872) under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France (1885–1925).

Louis Herbert Gray was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton University (~1892–1896) and Columbia University (~1896–1900, PhD), and held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

Louis Komjathy is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Boston University, studying under Paul Rouzer. As attested in 2014, he served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch. He held posts at the University of Lyon, Sorbonne, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Maison Franco-Japonaise.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden, including under Sylvain Lévi, and served as professor of comparative grammar at Ghent University (1893–1929).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès was an Orientalist in Sinology, Indology, and Iranian studies who studied at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy. He was administrator and Persian chair at INALCO (~1795–1824) and keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale (~1795–1824).

Louise A. Cort is a specialist in Japanology, history, and archaeology who studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, Oxford. She served as ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries (~1981–2020).

Louise Child specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds, supervised by Linda Hogan and receiving traditional instruction from Ringu Tulku, and subsequently taught there.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned her PhD from Gauhati University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and held a post there around 1986.

Luca Maria Olivieri is an archaeologist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at Freie Universität Berlin (attested 2010). He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~2011) and became Associate Professor at Ca' Foscari University (~2021).

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London, including Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and Associate Professor (attested 2015), as well as Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Lucia Galli is a Tibetologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Ernst Kuhn at Munich (Promotion). He served as a professor at the University of Munich (~1901–1936) and curator/director at the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907).

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1876–1879) and the Sorbonne (~1879–1884), and later held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927).

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and attended Paris, Leipzig, and ENLOV. He held academic posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1921–1924), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.
